Name: Aliens
Draw: Aliens are built wrong on purpose and nothing about them resolves into a human read. The trunk does not narrow into shoulders and there is no face holding anything together: eyes are on stalks, several of them, at different heights and lengths, and they do not all point the same way. Limbs come in the wrong count — three arms, five legs, a pair that matches nothing — and at least one of them is a tentacle, tapering, banded and clearly still moving. Surfaces are wet-looking chitin and soft membrane at once, in colours that have nothing to do with flesh: deep teal, bruised violet-grey, an oily iridescence along the edges. Every one of them is wearing something — a wrapped garment, a harness of plates, a fringe of hanging panels, a heavy collar — and the clothing is plainly made and plainly deliberate, and plainly not made for a human body: it fastens around the wrong parts and leaves openings for limbs a person does not have. Do not give them a face, do not give them shoulders, and do not settle them into a human stance.

ElementDraw.fire: The garments are orange and burning without being consumed. Hanging panels smoulder at the hems, thin smoke lifts out of the weave and drifts up past the eye stalks, and embers sit down in the folds like coals in a grate. The cloth is dull ember-orange in shadow and brightens to hot orange where the light reaches it. The creature's own skin stays whatever it is; what is orange and smoking is what it is wearing.
ElementDraw.ice: The garments are pale blue and fogged. Cold mist pours off the hems and pools around the base of the creature, the cloth is stiff with rime and frosted white along every fold, and condensation beads on the plates of the harness. Lit, the blue goes pale and watery; in shadow it is deep and glassy. The creature's own skin stays whatever it is; what is blue and foggy is what it is wearing.
ElementDraw.lightning: The garments are yellow and live. Arcs crawl along the seams and jump between the hanging panels and the harness plates, the cloth is shot through with bright yellow filaments that flicker rather than hold, and every fitting on it is pitted and haloed. Loose ends of the garment lift as though charged. The creature's own skin stays whatever it is; what is yellow and sparking is what it is wearing.
ElementDraw.earth: The garments have gone to rock. Green stone grows through the cloth in rough protrusions — slabs across the back, angular crystal pushing out of the harness, a fringe of broken mineral where a hem should be — and what fabric is left is dusty and dragged heavy by it. It stands lower than its siblings under the weight. The creature's own skin stays whatever it is; what is rocky and green is what it is wearing.
ElementDraw.arcane: The garments are purple and lit from inside. Light leaks out of the weave and out of every gap in the harness, throwing violet up onto the underside of the eye stalks and the limbs above it, and the hanging panels glow at their edges as though something is behind them. It is the only light in the picture that is not the key light. The creature's own skin stays whatever it is; what is purple and glowing is what it is wearing.

Records.Name: Specimen
Records.Draw: Something that was being kept and has got out. A slack upright trunk with four mismatched limbs, two of them tentacles, and a low crown of short eye stalks all swivelled onto the viewer at once. Its wrapped garment is torn open down one side and a cut length of tether still hangs from the collar. Upright but not braced — it has not decided what it is yet.

Records.Name: Survey Drone
Records.Draw: A squat hovering body with no legs at all, a ring of long thin eye stalks around its upper rim turning at different speeds, and three jointed arms folded underneath ending in instruments rather than hands. Its garment is a fitted band of hanging panels around the middle of the body, cut for a torso that is a sphere. It hangs slightly nose-down, measuring you.

Records.Name: Seeded Husk
Records.Draw: A hollowed body carrying something else's young. The trunk has split down the front and the gap is packed with translucent sacs; two long tentacles hold the split closed from either side and a third has gone slack. Only two eye stalks are left and one has drooped. Its garment is intact and neatly fastened, which is the worst part.

Records.Name: Abomination
Records.Draw: Too much of everything. Limbs in the wrong count, three of them tentacles, coming off a trunk with no clear front, and eye stalks in a disordered thicket rather than a row. It wears a harness built for something with half its limbs, buckled across it anyway and cutting into the flesh where the extra ones grew through.

Records.Name: The Watcher
Records.Draw: A tall narrow stalk of a creature that is almost entirely eyes. A slender trunk widens into a crown of long eye stalks, more than can be counted, fanned out and every one aimed forward. The two short tentacles below are folded and still. Its garment is a full-length robe of overlapping hanging panels running to the bottom of the picture, and the stalks come out of its collar.

Records.Name: Harvester
Records.Draw: Built to take things apart. A heavy forward-leaning trunk on four short legs, with two long tentacles and two rigid arms ending in curved cutting hooks, held out and open. A cluster of eye stalks sits low on the front of the body, below the arms, so it looks up at what it is working on. It wears a panelled apron, heavily stained.

Records.Name: Bio-Titan Toxoid
Records.Draw: A swollen giant. The trunk is a bloated sac overhanging a ring of short thick legs, its skin translucent over something that moves inside it, and four tentacles come off the upper body and drip steadily. The eye stalks are short and sunk into the swelling, barely clearing it. Its garment is a wide collar of plates around the top of the sac, far too small to cover what is under it.
Records.Title: the Flooded

Records.Name: Bio-Titan Plagueborn
Records.Draw: A giant coming apart into others. The main trunk is ridged and split in several places, and smaller limbs — half-formed tentacles, partial eye stalks, a hand with nothing behind it — push out of the splits the whole length of it. Its garment is wrapped round and round the trunk in bands, and the new limbs have torn through it at every height.
Records.Title: the Spreading

Records.Name: Bio-Titan Omega
Records.Draw: The largest and the only finished one. A tall trunk that reads symmetrical at a distance and resolves into nothing that matches: limbs in tiers down the body, the upper pair rigid and bladed, the lower pairs tentacles, and a single unbroken ring of long eye stalks at the top, evenly spaced and all open. It wears layered hanging panels from the ring down, cut cleanly and fitted exactly — the only one of them dressed on purpose.
Records.Title: the Last Word
